probes.note: Stolen credentials, public sign-up and password-reset flows, and identity-provider probing. Each request often used a different residential or ISP proxy exit.

ci-trust.note: Attacker-created branches abused CI workload identity trust. Harvest workflows dumped CI-accessible secrets and Terraform state.

node-collector.note: Privileged pods mounted the node root filesystem. The collector pod harvested kubelet PKI and projected service-account tokens. Wiz Sensor also saw nsenter and IMDS kube-env queries.

argo-admin.note: A cert-manager token could read ArgoCD secrets, and that read led to cluster-admin. This is the secret read, not proof a new binding was created.

csai.note: CyberStrikeAI ran this case. csai- names, an ARTEX checkout, and an auto-generated report are operator artifacts, not a victim tool-call audit.

tf-binding.note: A stolen Terraform-runner session read the kubelet kubeconfig and created a privileged pod and a cluster-admin binding.

jenkins-rootkit.note: Jenkins remote code execution opened a reverse shell. A pod escape placed an ld.so.preload rootkit disguised as a fontconfig service. The profile covers the persistence write, not the DNS-tunnel protocol.

offbox.note: Node, IRSA, and Terraform-runner credentials were used from the attacker server for Terraform state, Secrets Manager, and SSM sessions.

open-dir.note: The open directory showed forged identity-provider tokens, SSH private keys, GitHub Actions secrets, Anthropic API keys, and coding-assistant session histories.
